description: One function in the authorization package resolves the subject for a user (user type, teams, managed users, client portfolio), and the ticket, project, asset, document and credential paths all use it; no caller passes a hard-coded empty portfolio.
prdRefs: Segment A — Subject, portfolio and ownership foundations

description: A per-user client portfolio is stored in a tenant table (one row per user and client), registered in the tenant table manifest, with commands to set and clear it; a user with no rows has no portfolio.
prdRefs: Segment A — Subject, portfolio and ownership foundations

description: The `client_portfolio` template matches a record whose client is in the subject's stored portfolio, in both the record matcher and the SQL compiler, and denies when the portfolio is empty.
prdRefs: Segment A — Subject, portfolio and ownership foundations

description: The table manifest declares how each client-owned table reaches a client: a named column, or a parent chain of up to three hops, or a set of alternative parents; a contract test fails when a table with a foreign key to clients has no declaration or stated exemption.
prdRefs: Segment A — Subject, portfolio and ownership foundations

description: Client ownership for polymorphic tables (time entries, schedule entries, document associations, tag mappings) is resolved by a registered resolver per discriminator value, and an unknown discriminator resolves to no client.
prdRefs: Segment A — Subject, portfolio and ownership foundations

description: A tenant with no published bundle assignments and no portfolio rows runs zero additional queries on ticket list, ticket detail, client list, search and time-entry paths, recorded as query-budget entries.
prdRefs: Segment A — Subject, portfolio and ownership foundations

description: A failure to load bundle rules or resolve the subject denies access on the project, asset and document read paths, as it already does on the ticket path.
prdRefs: Segment B — Kernel semantics

description: A bundle revision can be published as closed: for every subject it is assigned to, a resource and action with no matching rule in that bundle is denied; an open bundle keeps today's behavior.
prdRefs: Segment B — Kernel semantics

description: When a subject holds a closed bundle and an open bundle, a resource and action the closed bundle does not name is denied.
prdRefs: Segment B — Kernel semantics

description: Creating a ticket, project, asset, contact, interaction, time entry or document association is evaluated by the kernel against the record to be created, so a client-restricted subject cannot create a record for a client outside their scope.
prdRefs: Segment B — Kernel semantics

description: Update and delete of a record are allowed only when the subject's read rules also allow that record.
prdRefs: Segment B — Kernel semantics

description: A package can register a built-in rule resolver for a class of subjects; rules from a registered resolver apply before bundle rules, can declare a closed baseline, and are not editable in policy administration; with no resolver registered behavior is unchanged.
prdRefs: Segment B — Kernel semantics

description: A denial names its cause in the decision reasons: the rule, the closed baseline, the portfolio, or a registered resolver.
prdRefs: Segment B — Kernel semantics

description: Client lists, client detail and client pickers return only in-scope clients for a client-restricted subject, with the restriction applied in SQL so counts and pagination match.
prdRefs: Segment C — Coverage of operational resources

description: Contact lists, contact detail and contact pickers return only contacts of in-scope clients for a client-restricted subject, and contacts with no client are hidden from them.
prdRefs: Segment C — Coverage of operational resources

description: Interaction lists and detail return only interactions of in-scope clients for a client-restricted subject.
prdRefs: Segment C — Coverage of operational resources

description: Time-entry lists, ticket time summaries and timesheet entry reads return only entries whose work item belongs to an in-scope client for a client-restricted subject; entries with no client are visible to their own user.
prdRefs: Segment C — Coverage of operational resources

description: On schedule and dispatch views a client-restricted subject sees an entry for an out-of-scope work item as busy time with no title or work item detail, and work item search returns only in-scope items.
prdRefs: Segment C — Coverage of operational resources

description: Document lists, folder trees, folder statistics and the distinct entity types offered as filters are computed over documents the subject may read.
prdRefs: Segment C — Coverage of operational resources

description: Tag lists and tag suggestions for a client-restricted subject are derived only from entities that subject may read.
prdRefs: Segment C — Coverage of operational resources

description: The ticket lookup and work-item lookup actions used by scheduling apply ticket read permission and narrowing.
prdRefs: Segment C — Coverage of operational resources

description: Project task comment reads and writes apply the project's authorization on both the server actions and the REST controller.
prdRefs: Segment C — Coverage of operational resources

description: For a client-restricted subject a ticket bundle shows only in-scope child tickets and their mirrored comments.
prdRefs: Segment C — Coverage of operational resources

description: Ticket form options and new-ticket data list internal users only as assignees, never portal users, and list tag text only from tickets the subject may read.
prdRefs: Segment D — Aggregates, options and exports

description: Counts and statistics shown on ticket, client, project and dashboard screens are computed over the records the subject may read.
prdRefs: Segment D — Aggregates, options and exports

description: A report run by a client-restricted subject applies their narrowing to client-owned tables in the report definition, and a report that cannot be narrowed is refused with a stated reason.
prdRefs: Segment D — Aggregates, options and exports

description: Client, contact, time-entry and ticket exports contain only records the subject may read.
prdRefs: Segment D — Aggregates, options and exports

description: Search resolves the client-restricted access mode for an internal subject whose rules restrict clients, instead of unrestricted access for every non-client user.
prdRefs: Segment E — Search

description: The client, contact, interaction, document and time-entry indexers set the record's client scope, and a repeatable per-tenant re-index fills existing rows.
prdRefs: Segment E — Search

description: Ticket search for a subject restricted to selected boards returns only tickets on those boards.
prdRefs: Segment E — Search

description: Records of strict types with no client scope are hidden from client-restricted subjects in search.
prdRefs: Segment E — Search

description: The REST controllers for clients, contacts, interactions, time entries, time sheets, document lists, project task comments and search apply the same permission, narrowing and create checks as the corresponding actions.
prdRefs: Segment F — REST and MCP parity

description: A bundle assigned to an API key narrows that key's requests on those controllers, and MCP search and endpoint calls made with the key return only in-scope records.
prdRefs: Segment F — REST and MCP parity

description: List totals and pagination on REST endpoints reflect the narrowed set, including when a rule redacts fields.
prdRefs: Segment F — REST and MCP parity

description: The MSP ticket, project and asset screens omit fields named in `redactedFields` the same way REST responses do.
prdRefs: Segment G — Field redaction parity

description: A contract test fails when an exported server action or REST handler reads a table whose ownership declaration maps to a covered resource without calling an authorization entry point; exceptions are pinned with a reason and the list cannot grow.
prdRefs: Segment H — Coverage contracts

description: A contract test pins every exported server action that touches tenant data without a permission check; the list cannot grow, and no pinned action may read a commercial table.
prdRefs: Segment H — Coverage contracts

description: Policy administration offers every resource type in the kernel catalog instead of a fixed list of six.
prdRefs: Segment I — Policy administration

description: An administrator edits a user's client portfolio on the user's record with the standard client picker; client names are shown, not identifiers.
prdRefs: Segment I — Policy administration

description: The bundle editor publishes a bundle as closed, marks closed bundles in the library, and previews the resource types a closed bundle will deny.
prdRefs: Segment I — Policy administration

description: The simulator explains a denial caused by a closed baseline, a portfolio, a create check or a read requirement on update.
prdRefs: Segment I — Policy administration

description: A starter bundle "Single-client technician" is available: closed, with `client_portfolio` rules for the operational resource types; and the duplicate starter-bundle definition on the server is removed so there is one source.
prdRefs: Segment I — Policy administration
